description: The answer to the question 'mandatory event without a handler: refusal or warning?': it is neither - the KERNEL does not refuse (ok=True, all the ops apply, no 'refused') and the VERIFY does not warn: it gives an ERROR and the module becomes invalid (isValid=False). Over job:block-events-reactive, OnRate becomes IsMandatory true and TWO new instances without a handler are born: TWO EventHandlerRequiredAction errors come out, one per instance, each on the path of its IEventHandler - the mandatoriness is charged per INSTANCE, not per block, and the already existing instance (RatingPicker1) stays clean. Note also that the instance without a handler ALREADY counts as a consumer of the event: the `usages` gives 4 (3 IEventHandler + 1 ITriggerNode), because the IEventHandler is born with the instance even if empty - that is why the delete of the event is refused even when nobody linked any handler (tests/jobs-negative/delete-block-event-in-use.json). The right path is in tests/jobs/block-events-two-instances-reactive.json: same IsMandatory true, one handler per instance, valid module.

expectedMessages.why: THIS is the result the job exists to prove: with IsMandatory true, the new instance without a handler produces an error (not a warning) on its own IEventHandler. Silencing this would be erasing the proof.
The second message is the proof that the charge is per INSTANCE and not per block nor per event: two instances without a handler give two errors, with different paths.

ops._why: before: the event is optional and has one consumer with a handler
1. make it mandatory - note that the OLD instance, which already has a handler, is not affected

ops.name: RatingPicker2
ops._why: 2. new instance WITHOUT a handler: the kernel accepts it without saying anything

ops.name: RatingPicker3
ops._why: 3. the third serves only to prove that the charge is per instance: there are two errors, not one
EventHandlers 1 even with no handler linked: the IEventHandler object is born with the instance, with the Handler left to fill
4 consumers: the two empty instances count as much as the one that has a handler
